title: Bayesian quant suggester playbook
body:
Status: draft
Owner: Maya Chen (product-optimize)
Contributors: Omar P., Lucia G., Anil R.

Purpose
--------
This note sketches a compact, reproducible approach for recommending per-model and per-route quantization configurations using a Bayesian decision layer over sampled cost/quality/latency profiles. Goal is a lightweight service that emits a small set of ranked recommendations (e.g., {INT8, FP8, 4-bit} + optional KV cache behavior) with calibrated uncertainty and conditional rules so SREs and customers can accept a recommendation with clear risk bounds.

Why a Bayesian layer?
---------------------
- Quantization outcomes vary with model architecture, token distribution, prompt length, and output temperature. Point estimates (single-cost/single-accuracy numbers) hide this uncertainty.
- A Bayes-aware recommender produces a posterior over expected quality loss and latency uplift, enabling risk-conditioned choices (e.g., "choose FP8 if P(recall drop > 1%) < 0.05").
- Supports efficient exploration: the system can suggest conservative starting configs for production and targeted experiments for high-payoff routes.

High-level approach
--------------------
1) Offline calibration stage: run a limited factorial experiment sampling bitwidths (4-bit, INT8, FP8), activation quantization knobs, and representative prompt/response pairs per route. Capture: token cost per request, P50/P95 latency, and quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/LLR/acceptance-rate) and a small set of model logits-based fidelity measures.
2) Fit hierarchical Bayesian models that share strength across similar routes/models. Observations: cost ~ deterministic (cheap), latency ~ skewed (log-normal-ish), quality delta ~ heavy tailed. Use priors informed by microbench results.
3) At recommendation time: given route metadata (avg prompt len, output len, temperature, cached-prefix hit rate, SLA constraints), produce posterior predictive distributions for cost/latency/quality under each candidate quant config.
4) Rank candidates by constrained utility (maximize cost reduction subject to constraints on quality loss and latency SLOs). Provide the top-3 with calibrated P-values and recommended rollout steps (canary %, monitoring alarms).

Model details (simple, interpretable)
-----------------------------------
- Notation: y_q = observed quality delta (baseline FP16 -> candidate), l_q = latency delta, c_q = cost ratio.
- Likelihood choices: y_q ~ StudentT(mu_y, sigma_y, nu) to handle outliers; log(l_q + 1) ~ Normal(mu_l, sigma_l); log(c_q) ~ Normal(mu_c, sigma_c) (cost mostly deterministic so small sigma_c).
- Hierarchical structure: mu_y_route ~ Normal(mu_y_model_family, tau_family), mu_y_model_family ~ Normal(mu_y_global, tau_global). Same hierarchy for latency.
- Priors seeded from microbench: mu_c_global centered on observed token-cost multipliers per quant mode; sigma_c small (0.01-0.05).

Input features for per-route posterior prediction
------------------------------------------------
- model_family (gpt-like-7b, llama2-13b, etc.)
- avg_prompt_tokens, avg_completion_tokens
- temperature, top_p (sampling intensity)
- kv_prefix_cache_hit_rate
- avg_target_length_variance (controls latency tail)
- training-time calibration dataset (small id for route-specific evals)

Outputs (per-candidate)
-----------------------
- posterior mean and 95% credible interval for: quality delta (relative to baseline), P(failure_quality_threshold), P95 latency, expected tokens-per-request cost
- recommended rollout recipe: default canary% (3%), increased monitoring windows, suggested eval set to push to canary
- a simple "risk score" (0-10) derived from probability of violating constraints and expected customer impact

Decision logic / ranking
-------------------------
We compute constrained utility: U = E[cost_savings] - lambda * E[quality_loss_cost], where lambda is calibrated from product-ops policy and customer impact heuristics. Then filter by latency SLO: discard candidates with P(P95_latency > SLA) > 0.02. Rank remaining by U. Provide top 3 and a conservative fallback (e.g., keep FP16 or INT8 with activation-range-preserve).

Mini simulation (toy numbers, illustrative)
-----------------------------------------
- Baseline FP16 tokens-per-request: $0.012
- INT8 expected tokens-per-request: $0.007 (CI: [$0.0068,$0.0072])
- FP8 expected tokens-per-request: $0.0085 (CI: [$0.0080,$0.0090])
- 4-bit expected tokens-per-request: $0.0055 (high variance CI: [$0.0040,$0.0075])
- Baseline P95 latency: 140 ms; SLA target: 160 ms
Posterior predictive for 4-bit: P(P95 > SLA) = 0.35 -> filter out for routes with strict SLA.
For a long-tail-search route (avg completion 40 tokens): INT8 yields 40% cost reduction, expected quality delta median 0.6% (P(>1%)=0.12). Recommendation: INT8 canary 5%, monitor quality metric specific to route; FP8 recommended only for noisy-generation routes with permissive latency SLOs.

Monitoring + rollout recipes (practical)
--------------------------------------
- Canary plan: 1) small canary (1-3%) for 24–72h capturing quality metrics and full request traces; 2) expand to 10–20% for 3–5 days if no regression; 3) stage to 50% with automated rollback on signal.
- Required alarms: P(failure_quality_threshold) > 0.05, P95 latency exceed SLA by 10% for 1h, error rate > baseline + 2σ.
- Suggested dashboards: per-route 1h/24h cost delta, rolling-window quality impact, tail latency heatmap, sample responses diff tool (labels for human review).

Experiment plan & data budget
----------------------------
- Minimal offline sample: 200 representative prompt/response pairs per route per quant candidate to estimate initial posterior; prioritize high-traffic routes.
- If route is low-traffic: borrow hierarchy priors from model family and use a smaller route-specific sample (n=50) for quick calibration.
- Experiment storage: store logits, predicted tokens, raw responses, and latency traces for offline analysis (privacy note: redact customer PII).

API surface (proposal)
----------------------
- /recommend-quant-config (POST): payload includes route_id, recent usage stats (avg lengths, cache hit-rate), SLA object, utility weights; returns top-3 candidates with posterior summaries and rollout recipe.
- /submit-calibration-batch (POST): upload a small batch of labeled prompts/evals to refine the posterior for a route.
- /explain-decision (GET): returns the variables that drove the recommendation and the minimal test to reduce uncertainty (e.g., "run 150 sample prompts with temp=0.9 to disambiguate FP8 vs INT8").

Open questions / risks
----------------------
- Quality metrics: route-specific metrics are crucial. Global proxies (BLEU, log-likelihood) sometimes correlate poorly with perceived quality; need product-ops to declare primary metric per route.
- Cost model drift: token pricing or hardware changes update the cost priors; propose scheduled re-calibration (monthly) and immediate trigger on price changes.
- Cold-start routes: hierarchy works but may under-estimate route-specific quirks (e.g., heavy use of long-context prompts). Must flag low-confidence results and require longer canaries.

Next steps (short roadmap)
-------------------------
- Week 0–2: prototype offline calibration scripts and a small factorial experiment on 6 representative routes (search, assistant, summarization, translation, reranking, code-gen). (Owner: Omar)
- Week 2–4: fit simple hierarchical models (PyMC3 or lightweight Laplace approx in JAX/NumPyro) and produce per-candidate posterior reports for those 6 routes. (Owner: Lucia)
- Week 4–6: implement lightweight API wrapper (recommend-quant-config) and a canary runner that automates rollout recipes and monitoring hooks. (Owner: Anil)
- Week 6–8: run internal purple-team review with SRE/product-ops and iterate thresholds.

Appendix: example output (JSON-ish, human readable)
---------------------------------------------------
- candidate: INT8
  - quality_delta_median: 0.6%
  - quality_delta_95ci: [0.1%, 1.3%]
  - P(quality_loss > 1%): 0.12
  - expected_cost_per_request: $0.007 (CI [$0.0068,$0.0072])
  - P95_latency_median: 150ms (CI [140, 165])
  - P(P95_latency > SLA 160ms): 0.08
  - rollout: canary 5%, monitor route_metric_1, rollback if P(quality_loss>1%) > 0.05

Notes for implementers
----------------------
- Keep the recommendation engine lightweight: avoid full MCMC in the online path. Use cached posterior summaries and cheap posterior predictive draws via Laplace or variational approximations; perform full MCMC in offline re-calibration windows.
- Expose uncertainty to users explicitly—show credible intervals and an explanation string rather than a single-score black box.
- Prioritize safety: always include a conservative fallback and automated rollback triggers in any recommended recipe.
